activities.title: Apply for a SIN
activities.summary: Your Social Insurance Number — required to work and access benefits

tasks.title: Gather your documents
tasks.description: Bring your passport plus your work permit, study permit, or PR card. If any document is not in English or French, bring a certified translation.

tasks.title: Apply through Service Canada
tasks.description: Apply online at Canada.ca, by mail, or in person at a Service Canada Centre. In-person applications usually issue your SIN the same day.

tasks.title: Confirm your SIN letter
tasks.description: You'll receive a confirmation of SIN letter rather than a physical card. Keep this letter somewhere safe — you'll need it for payroll and benefits forms.

tasks.title: Protect your SIN
tasks.description: Only share your SIN with employers, financial institutions, and government agencies that are legally required to ask for it.

activities.title: Get a Health Card
activities.summary: Provincial health coverage so medical visits are covered

tasks.title: Check your waiting period
tasks.description: Some provinces apply a waiting period (often up to 3 months) before coverage starts. Check the MSI website for NS's current rules, and consider private interim health insurance to cover the gap.

tasks.title: Gather proof of identity and status
tasks.description: You'll typically need your passport, immigration document (PR card, work or study permit), and proof you live in NS, such as a lease or utility bill.

tasks.title: Apply for your MSI
tasks.description: Submit your application to MSI, either online, by mail, or in person, depending on what your province offers.

tasks.title: Carry your card once it arrives
tasks.description: Bring your MSI to every medical appointment. Without it, clinics may charge you directly for visits.
